text.p: Whatever he is known as in the future, Fenerbahce's Uche Okechukwu will have every reason to remember the goal he scored against Trabzonspor on Sunday because it earned him a bonus of $10,000.
Okechukwu's match-winner was the 2,000th goal in the club's history and could be one of the last he scores under his present identity.

Okechukwu, a Nigerian, and club mate and compatriot Augustine "Jay Jay" Okocha are planning to become Turkish citizens and will be known as Abdulkerim Rahim Uche and Muhammed Yavuz Okocha respectively.
But Fenerbahce's joy at beating Trabzonspor quickly evaporated because of injuries to key players ahead of Wednesday's European Champions' League match against Manchester United in England.

Danish defender Jes Hogh aggrevated an old groin injury against Trabzonspor, while Bulgarian forward Emil Kostadinov, free to play against United after suspension, and midfielder Bulent Uygun are also suffering groin strains.
Because of the uncertainty surrounding the injured players, Fenerbahce took a squad of 20 to Manchester on Monday.

But Fenerbahce chairman Ali Sen was upbeat: "We showed some good football during the Trabzonspor match," he said. "Now we are looking to the Champions' League. We are going to show everyone that all is not over yet.

"I believe we are going to put on an incredible performance on Wednesday. Our players are going to go down in history... We owe Turkey a win. All Turks are going to go out on the streets in celebration on Wednesday night."
Manchester United beat Fenerbahce in Istanbul 2-0 two weeks ago and have never been beaten at home in 40 years of European competition.
